title: How much Google Ads cost in India, and how to set a budget
excerpt: Google Ads has no fixed price or minimum spend. What it costs depends on clicks, competition and goals. Learn how to estimate a monthly budget for your own business.
author: Marketix Studio
metaTitle: How Much Google Ads Cost in India | Marketix Studio
metaDescription: Google Ads has no minimum spend. Learn what drives cost per click in India, how to estimate a monthly budget, GST, agency fees and how long approval takes.
secondaryKeywords: how much google ads cost per month
how much time google ads take to approve

paragraphs: Google Ads has no fixed price and no minimum spend in India. You set a daily budget, and you are charged mainly when someone clicks your ad, at a price decided by a live auction. So how much Google Ads cost for a business depends on its industry, city, competition and how many leads or sales it needs each month.

Below, we cover what drives the cost of a click, how to estimate a monthly budget using free tools inside Google Ads, what Google and an agency each charge, and how long it takes for ads to get approved and start delivering.

sections.heading: Key takeaways
points: Work backwards from the number of leads or sales you need, then from your conversion rate, to arrive at a budget. Never pick a round number first.
Check Keyword Planner bid ranges for your exact city and service before committing money. They differ a lot between categories.
Plan for GST on top of ad spend, and for an agency or freelancer fee if someone else runs the account.
Treat the first month as paid research. Judge cost per lead only after the account has some conversion data.
Fix the landing page and lead follow-up before raising the budget. A weak page makes every click more expensive.

sections.heading: How much do Google Ads cost in India?
paragraphs: There is no rate card. Each click is priced by an auction, and the price you pay is set by how much competitors are bidding and how relevant Google judges your ad to be.

Quality Score matters more than most owners expect. Two businesses bidding on the same keyword can pay very different amounts per click if one has a closely matched ad and a fast, relevant page. A dedicated page built for the campaign, such as the ones covered under [Landing Pages & Funnels](/services/landing-pages-funnels), tends to help on both cost and conversion.

High-ticket categories like real estate, education, healthcare and legal services see heavier bidding because each customer is worth a lot. A local bakery or salon in a smaller locality may face far less competition for the same kind of search.
The main factors that push the cost of a click up or down:
points: How competitive the keyword is in your category
The city or area you target, since metros attract more bidders
How much a customer is worth to competitors in that space
Your Quality Score, which looks at expected click-through rate, ad relevance and landing page experience
The time of day, device and audience you choose
The campaign type, since Search, Display, YouTube and Performance Max behave differently

sections.heading: How much do Google Ads cost per month, and how do I estimate it?
paragraphs: A sensible monthly budget comes from your targets, not a guess. Decide how many leads or sales you need, estimate what each click will cost, and estimate how many clicks it takes to get one lead.

You can get a real figure for your own case for free. Google's [Keyword Planner](https://support.google.com/google-ads/answer/7337243) shows the low and high range of top-of-page bids for your keywords, filtered by location. Website analytics or past campaigns can tell you roughly what share of visitors enquire. With no history at all, a small fixed test budget run for a few weeks gives the business real numbers to work from.

Example: a dental clinic wants 50 enquiries a month. Keyword Planner shows bids for its main keywords in its city sitting around ₹40 per click. If roughly 5 in every 100 visitors enquire, it needs about 1,000 clicks. That works out to around ₹40,000 a month in ad spend, before GST. These numbers are round and purely illustrative; real bids for dentists in any given city may be quite different.

For eCommerce, the same logic runs on sales and order value. Work out how much revenue each rupee of ad spend must return to stay profitable, which our guide on [break-even ROAS](/blog/break-even-roas-calculation) walks through step by step.

sections.heading: Do Google Ads cost money if nobody clicks?
paragraphs: Yes, Google Ads costs money, but on Search campaigns you are normally charged only when someone clicks. If your ad is shown and nobody clicks, that impression costs nothing.

Some campaign types can bill differently. Display and YouTube campaigns can be set up to charge per thousand impressions or per view, and certain bid strategies let you target a cost per conversion. Even then, the money comes out of the budget you set, and you can pause or stop at any time.

The [actual cost per click](https://support.google.com/google-ads/answer/6297) is often lower than your maximum bid. You pay only what is needed to hold your position in that auction, which is why bids and final charges rarely match exactly.

sections.heading: How much does Google charge, and what does an agency charge on top?
paragraphs: Google charges only for the ad spend itself. There is no account fee or setup fee from Google. In India, invoices are raised with GST added on top, so budget for tax over and above the spend you see in the dashboard.

One rule surprises many owners. On a given day, Google may spend up to twice your average daily budget if traffic is good, but over a month it will not charge more than your daily budget multiplied by the average number of days in a month. Google explains this in its help page on [average daily budgets](https://support.google.com/google-ads/answer/2375454).

If an agency or freelancer manages the account, their fee is separate from ad spend. Whichever model a brand picks, the Google Ads account should be in its own name, with the owner holding admin access. You can see how we structure management fees on our [Pricing](/pricing) page.
Common fee structures include:
points: Fixed retainer: a set monthly fee regardless of spend, common for smaller accounts
Percentage of ad spend: the fee rises as the budget grows
Hybrid: a base fee plus a smaller percentage above a spend level
Performance-linked: part of the fee tied to agreed lead or sales targets

sections.heading: How much time do Google Ads take to approve and start running?
paragraphs: Most ads are reviewed within one business day, according to Google's [ad review process](https://support.google.com/adspolicy/answer/1722120). Some take longer, especially in restricted categories such as healthcare, finance or gambling, or when the account is new.

Ads can start showing within hours of approval. Stable, predictable results take longer. Smart Bidding strategies need conversion data before they perform well, so the first few weeks are often uneven, and a business that changes bids and budgets every other day keeps resetting that learning.
Getting from zero to a live, stable campaign has a few stages:
points: Create the account and add billing details, either automatic payments or prepaid manual payments
Complete advertiser verification if Google asks for it, which can add some days
Set up conversion tracking so you can measure enquiries or purchases
Build campaigns, keywords, ads and landing pages
Submit for review and wait for approval
Allow a learning period while automated bidding gathers data

faqs.q: Is there a minimum budget for Google Ads in India?
faqs.a: No. Google does not set a minimum spend, so you can start with whatever daily budget you choose. In practice, a budget too small to buy a reasonable number of clicks will not give you enough data to judge whether the campaign works.

faqs.q: Why was I charged more than my daily budget on one day?
faqs.a: Google can spend up to twice your average daily budget on days when traffic is strong. Over the month, total charges stay within your daily budget multiplied by the average days in a month, so busy days balance out against quieter ones.

faqs.q: Is GST charged on Google Ads in India?
faqs.a: Yes. Google adds GST to Google Ads invoices for Indian advertisers. A GST-registered business can enter its GSTIN in billing settings so invoices carry it, which helps when claiming input tax credit with your accountant.

faqs.q: How long before Google Ads bring in leads?
faqs.a: Clicks can start the same day ads are approved, and enquiries can follow soon after. Consistent cost per lead takes a few weeks, since the account needs conversion data and some testing of keywords and ads.

faqs.q: Will I be charged after I pause my campaigns?
faqs.a: No new costs build up once campaigns are paused or removed. You may still see a charge for clicks that happened before the pause, because billing runs on a cycle and can lag behind actual activity.

faqs.q: Can I run Google Ads without a website?
faqs.a: Some formats allow it, such as call ads or campaigns that send people to a Google Business Profile. For most lead and sales goals, a focused landing page gives you better tracking, a better Quality Score and lower cost per lead.
